title: Streetcar sightseeing band and playing the French Market
summary: The brothers and Emmett Rogers play on a sightseeing car, earn tips and play for butchers.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, is that right? I didn't know. Anything else you can remember when you were a kid? Any of the first music you ever heard aside from home? Were there other bands around?
Well, there was a band on a color band called Sweet Buddy Petit. There was, Papa Lane used to call his band the Reliance band. And then we played on a streetcar, Emmet Rogers.
Oh yeah, tell me about that.

And Abby, we had a uniform. Abby had leader, I had manager, and Emmet Rogers on the drums had Brunis on his hat. And we used to play in a sightseeing car. We made good money. We used to point out the interesting points of New Orleans, these three guys. And then we'd play, you know, like harmony and stuff. Then Rogers would go through with the hat, passing the hat through the thing. We made $15, $20 a day.
He'd sit at one end of the car, stand at one end of the car and play there.

So one day we sent Rogers out for coffee and he got all excited and laughed and he happened to... His nose went into the coffee, you know. We wouldn't drink it so that's how we'd give him the name of Snotsy Rogers. Oh yeah. That's what the name of Snotsy Rogers we used to call. That's a good name.
That's a good name. I believe it was something... Boy, if you could only make money in that town, it's fabulous.
Do you remember playing at the French market? Abby said you'd...
We used to put the celery and what's the name, and our lapels. Yeah. Played for the butchers over there.
Go right into the French market, the stalls there?
Well we played like the unemployed bands in England, you know. Yeah.
Play on the corner. Did you take up a collection then too? Have a hat?

Well we didn't do it but they'd hand us money, you know. They figured we were unemployed or poor as them. It was all kicks those days, we didn't care. We didn't figure things would be like the other day.
I wish I knew then I'd be worth a million.
